name: SIG/BG
tagline: Which inputs separate signal from background, and which only appear to

intro.problem: The networks are only as good as their inputs, yet each input list was chosen before the current signal and background files existed. Some variables separate the samples because of physics; others separate them only because of how each sample was selected, and a ranking cannot tell the two apart on its own.
intro.value: A per-feature map of separation, region dependence and redundancy, with every selection effect flagged, gives the network-input work a trustworthy starting pool. It tells the barrel and endcap programs where the two regions carry different physics, and it hands the feature-competition game candidate sets that are already screened.
intro.approach: A public pipeline scores every shared column with the two-sample Kolmogorov–Smirnov distance [@smirnov1948] per region and mass point, against its own noise floor. Spearman correlation on background [@spearman1904] groups redundant features into blocks, and a gradient-boosted surrogate [@friedman2001] scores candidate input sets, with distance correlation [@szekely2007] between the two networks' surrogate scores.
intro.goals: A companion site where every plot is viewable and downloadable, the full development history is kept, and the excluded-feature list is editable; data-health checks that inform without removing features; and screened candidate pools handed to GAMBIT, which makes the final choice [@guyon2003].

questions: Which input variables separate signal from background in each region, and which only appear to because of how the samples were selected?
Where do the barrel and endcap differ in shape or in separation, so that a model trained in one region may carry the wrong physics into the other?
Which features are redundant with each other, and which strong separators do the current network input lists leave out?

components.name: Data health and inventory
components.subtitle: Block 00 · informational unit tests
components.summary: Every column in every input file is inventoried, duplicates are collapsed, exclusions are reported line by line, and the region split is audited. Data-health checks report pass or fail and never remove a feature; only the column rules (missing from a file, non-numeric, constant, duplicate, hard-excluded) drop one.

items.label: Selection
items.detail: A unit test checks the selection that defines each sample, because any variable tied to that selection separates the samples by construction

items.label: Exclusions
items.detail: One editable file of names or globs; the site can build a new one and download it

components.name: Separation and region maps
components.subtitle: Blocks A and B
components.summary: For each feature, the KS distance between signal and background in the endcap, the barrel and both, per mass point and combined with equal weight per mass point [@smirnov1948]. A separate map compares barrel and endcap shapes for background and for signal.

items.label: Noise floor
items.detail: Each distance is judged against the KS critical value for its sample sizes

items.label: Flags
items.detail: Selection-linked, jet-activity-dependent and non-physics features are marked in every ranking, and a feature that separates almost perfectly at a single mass point is marked suspicious

components.name: Correlation and candidate sets
components.subtitle: Blocks C and D · nominate, not decide
components.summary: Background rank correlation defines redundancy blocks [@spearman1904]. Four candidate input sets, from the current lists to an inclusive set, are scored by a gradient-boosted surrogate with five-fold cross-validation [@friedman2001]: separation per network role, the worst mass point, and dependence between the two roles [@szekely2007]. The surrogate nominates; GAMBIT decides on closure.

items.label: Hand-off
items.detail: Unit-test results, candidate pools per region, redundancy blocks, drop suggestions and the prototype lists, written as GAMBIT inputs

components.name: Companion site
components.subtitle: Public, static, every plot downloadable
components.summary: The site shows every feature page, ranking, correlation block and candidate set, every page of every PDF the work produced, and an archive of every earlier script version and run, unchanged. The code is public and runs on anyone's own copy of the files.

links.title: Feature competition
links.text: SIG/BG screens and nominates; GAMBIT takes the candidate pools and blocks and decides the partition on closure.

links.title: Barrel program
links.text: The barrel-versus-endcap maps show where the two regions carry different physics, which bears directly on pretraining a barrel model on the endcap.

links.title: Data-health checks
links.text: The informational unit tests here are the same kind of alert-not-stop checks BASELINE runs on its own files.
